items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The number of unemployed people as a percentage of the labour force"?
items.answer: unemployment rate
items.markingKey: B. This is the definition of unemployment rate.

items.stem: Explain why an average national unemployment rate may hide important differences.
items.answer: Unemployment varies by region, age, gender, ethnicity and skill; for example youth unemployment is often double the national rate.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Unemployment varies by region, age, gender, ethnicity and skill; for example youth unemployment is often double the national rate. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why the unemployment rate can fall even when the number of people in work does not increase.
items.answer: If unemployed people stop searching (discouraged workers) or leave the labour force, the number counted as unemployed falls, lowering the rate without any job creation.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: If unemployed people stop searching (discouraged workers) or leave the labour force, the number counted as unemployed falls, lowering the rate without any job creation. (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Outline one way in which India's informal labour market shows difficulties in measuring unemployment.
items.answer: Around 80-90% of India's workforce is estimated to work in the informal economy. Informal and self-employed work is difficult to record, so open unemployment rates appear low while underemployment is widespread
items.markingKey: Context (Around 80-90% of India's workforce is estimated to work in the informal economy.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Informal and self-employed work is difficult to record, so open unemployment rates appear low while underemployment is widespread – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to difficulties in measuring unemployment.

items.stem: Using Spain's youth unemployment as an example, explain differences hidden by the national unemployment rate.
items.answer: Spain's youth (under-25) unemployment rate peaked at over 55% in 2013 when the overall rate was about 26%. Young people with less experience and on temporary contracts were hit hardest, so the average understated their situation
items.markingKey: Context (Spain's youth (under-25) unemployment rate peaked at over 55% in 2013 when the overall rate was about 26%.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Young people with less experience and on temporary contracts were hit hardest, so the average understated their situation – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to differences hidden by the national unemployment rate.

items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of the view that the official unemployment rate is an accurate measure of spare capacity in the labour market.
items.answer: It is a useful headline indicator but should be read together with underemployment, participation and broader measures.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: based on internationally comparable ILO definition; regular and timely surveys; tracks cyclical changes well. Arguments against: excludes discouraged and underemployed workers; ignores informal work; averages hide regional and youth differences; sample survey errors. Supported judgement: It is a useful headline indicator but should be read together with underemployment, participation and broader measures.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "labour force".
items.answer: The number of people of working age who are employed or unemployed and seeking work

items.stem: Briefly explain why unemployment statistics may be inaccurate in economies with a large informal sector.
items.answer: Many people work informally in unrecorded jobs or are underemployed in subsistence activities, so surveys and official records poorly capture who is working or seeking work.

items.stem: What is likely to reduce frictional unemployment?
items.answer: Improved information about job vacancies through online job platforms

items.stem: Explain the difference between structural unemployment and frictional unemployment.
items.answer: Frictional unemployment is short-term job search by people with employable skills; structural unemployment is longer-term, due to skills or location mismatch with available jobs.

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why minimum wage legislation may increase structural unemployment.
items.answer: If the minimum wage is set above the equilibrium wage for low-skilled labour, quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, so some workers cannot find jobs. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "cyclical (demand-deficient) unemployment"?
options: The rate of unemployment that exists when the labour market is in equilibrium at potential output; the sum of frictional, structural and seasonal unemployment
The difficulty workers face in moving between occupations because they lack the skills required
The number of unemployed people as a percentage of the labour force
Unemployment caused by a fall in aggregate demand during the contraction phase of the business cycle
items.answer: Unemployment caused by a fall in aggregate demand during the contraction phase of the business cycle
items.markingKey: D. "cyclical (demand-deficient) unemployment" is unemployment caused by a fall in aggregate demand during the contraction phase of the business cycle.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "frictional unemployment"?
options: Short-term unemployment of people moving between jobs or entering the labour market and searching for work
Unemployment caused by a mismatch between workers' skills or locations and the jobs available, often due to changes in the structure of the economy, technology or labour market rigidities
Unemployment not captured by official statistics, such as discouraged workers who have stopped looking and underemployed workers
The output that could have been produced by unemployed workers, shown as a point inside the PPC
items.answer: Short-term unemployment of people moving between jobs or entering the labour market and searching for work
items.markingKey: A. "frictional unemployment" is short-term unemployment of people moving between jobs or entering the labour market and searching for work.

items.stem: A town loses 3,000 jobs when its car plant closes. Identify two costs to the local community and two costs to the government, and explain how hysteresis could make the problem persist.

items.markingKey: LF = 39,418; (i) 1,774/39,418 = 4.5%; (ii) 39,418/60,643 = 65.0%. [M1] for correct method/working; [A1] for both rates. Award [A1] only with correct units/notation where relevant.

items.stem: Outline one way in which long-term unemployment in Greece shows the costs of long-term unemployment.
items.answer: In 2014 about 70% of Greece's unemployed had been out of work for over a year, and youth unemployment exceeded 50%. Long spells eroded skills and attachment to the labour market, raising the risk of hysteresis and permanent loss of potential output
items.markingKey: Context (In 2014 about 70% of Greece's unemployed had been out of work for over a year, and youth unemployment exceeded 50%.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Long spells eroded skills and attachment to the labour market, raising the risk of hysteresis and permanent loss of potential output – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the costs of long-term unemployment.

items.stem: "Structural unemployment can be solved by cutting interest rates." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Lower rates raise AD and reduce cyclical unemployment, but structural unemployment requires supply-side measures such as retraining and improving labour mobility.
items.markingKey: Lower rates raise AD and reduce cyclical unemployment, but structural unemployment requires supply-side measures such as retraining and improving labour mobility. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Outline two points that could be used to evaluate the claim: "The official unemployment rate is an accurate measure of spare capacity in the labour market."
items.answer: It is a useful headline indicator but should be read together with underemployment, participation and broader measures.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: based on internationally comparable ILO definition; regular and timely surveys; tracks cyclical changes well. Arguments against: excludes discouraged and underemployed workers; ignores informal work; averages hide regional and youth differences; sample survey errors. Supported judgement: It is a useful headline indicator but should be read together with underemployment, participation and broader measures.

items.stem: You are an adviser to the central bank. A minister argues that the costs of unemployment are mainly economic rather than social. Using your knowledge of economics, write a policy recommendation that evaluates this view and recommends a course of action.
items.answer: The social costs are at least as serious and are often longer lasting; both justify policies to keep unemployment low.
items.markingKey: Supporting points: lost output and lower GDP; lower tax revenue and higher benefits; lost human capital. Counter-points: mental and physical health problems; crime and social exclusion; family breakdown; intergenerational effects. Recommendation: The social costs are at least as serious and are often longer lasting; both justify policies to keep unemployment low. items.stem: You are a policy adviser to the ministry of finance. A minister argues that supply-side policies are the most effective way to reduce unemployment. Using your knowledge of economics, write a policy recommendation that evaluates this view and recommends a course of action.
items.answer: The best policy depends on the type of unemployment: demand management for cyclical, supply-side for structural and frictional unemployment.
items.markingKey: Supporting points: tackle structural and frictional unemployment; raise potential output without inflation; long-lasting effects. Counter-points: ineffective against cyclical unemployment; long time lags; costly to the government; market-based reforms may increase inequality. Recommendation: The best policy depends on the type of unemployment: demand management for cyclical, supply-side for structural and frictional unemployment. items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The difficulty workers face in moving between occupations because they lack the skills required"?
items.answer: occupational immobility
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of occupational immobility.

items.stem: Which of the following people is counted as unemployed in a labour force survey?
options: A graduate actively applying for jobs who has not found one
A full-time student not seeking work
A worker on paid sick leave
items.answer: A graduate actively applying for jobs who has not found one
items.markingKey: A. Must be without work, available and actively seeking work.

items.stem: Define the term "hysteresis".
items.answer: The effect by which long periods of cyclical unemployment raise the natural rate, as unemployed workers lose skills and motivation
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the effect by which long periods of cyclical unemployment raise the natural rate, as unemployed workers lose skills and motivation. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain why frictional unemployment can never be eliminated completely.
items.answer: There will always be people changing jobs, entering the labour force or relocating, and it takes time to search and match with suitable vacancies.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: There will always be people changing jobs, entering the labour force or relocating, and it takes time to search and match with suitable vacancies. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A student claims that a falling unemployment rate always means the labour market is getting healthier. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: It may fall because discouraged workers leave the labour force, or because of rising underemployment in part-time jobs.
items.markingKey: It may fall because discouraged workers leave the labour force, or because of rising underemployment in part-time jobs. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why unemployment can increase income inequality.
items.answer: Unemployment is concentrated among low-skilled and young workers, whose income falls to benefits (if any), widening the gap with those in work.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Unemployment is concentrated among low-skilled and young workers, whose income falls to benefits (if any), widening the gap with those in work. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why technological change can cause structural unemployment.
items.answer: Automation reduces demand for some skills (e.g. routine manufacturing, checkout operators) while increasing demand for others; workers who lack the new skills or live in the wrong place cannot fill new vacancies.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Automation reduces demand for some skills (e.g. routine manufacturing, checkout operators) while increasing demand for others; workers who lack the new skills or live in the wrong place cannot fill new vacancies. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: "A falling unemployment rate always means the labour market is getting healthier." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: It may fall because discouraged workers leave the labour force, or because of rising underemployment in part-time jobs.

items.stem: Explain the difference between the natural rate of unemployment and cyclical unemployment.
items.answer: The natural rate is the unemployment that exists when output is at potential (frictional and structural); cyclical unemployment is the extra unemployment caused by a deflationary gap.
items.markingKey: The natural rate is the unemployment that exists when output is at potential (frictional and structural); cyclical unemployment is the extra unemployment caused by a deflationary gap. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: With reference to job losses in the USA in 2009, explain how it illustrates cyclical unemployment.
items.answer: US unemployment rose from 5% in early 2008 to 10% in October 2009 as AD collapsed after the financial crisis. Falling consumer and investment spending reduced the derived demand for labour across most sectors
items.markingKey: Context (US unemployment rose from 5% in early 2008 to 10% in October 2009 as AD collapsed after the financial crisis.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Falling consumer and investment spending reduced the derived demand for labour across most sectors – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to cyclical unemployment.

items.stem: With reference to Spain's youth unemployment, explain how it illustrates differences hidden by the national unemployment rate.
items.answer: Spain's youth (under-25) unemployment rate peaked at over 55% in 2013 when the overall rate was about 26%. Young people with less experience and on temporary contracts were hit hardest, so the average understated their situation
items.markingKey: Context (Spain's youth (under-25) unemployment rate peaked at over 55% in 2013 when the overall rate was about 26%.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Young people with less experience and on temporary contracts were hit hardest, so the average understated their situation – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to differences hidden by the national unemployment rate.

items.stem: Briefly describe the fall in US labour force participation after 2008 and explain what it reveals about hysteresis and hidden costs of unemployment.
items.answer: US labour force participation fell from about 66% in 2008 to about 63% by 2015. Some long-term unemployed workers left the labour force entirely, reducing potential output
items.markingKey: Context (US labour force participation fell from about 66% in 2008 to about 63% by 2015.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Some long-term unemployed workers left the labour force entirely, reducing potential output – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to hysteresis and hidden costs of unemployment.

items.stem: Using tourism employment in Thailand as an example, explain seasonal and demand-deficient unemployment.
items.answer: Thailand's tourism employment fluctuates between high and low seasons, and collapsed in 2020 when international arrivals fell by over 80%. Normal seasonal swings were overtaken by a large fall in demand, adding cyclical unemployment
items.markingKey: Context (Thailand's tourism employment fluctuates between high and low seasons, and collapsed in 2020 when international arrivals fell by over 80%.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Normal seasonal swings were overtaken by a large fall in demand, adding cyclical unemployment – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to seasonal and demand-deficient unemployment.

items.stem: With reference to India's informal labour market, explain how it illustrates difficulties in measuring unemployment.
items.answer: Around 80-90% of India's workforce is estimated to work in the informal economy. Informal and self-employed work is difficult to record, so open unemployment rates appear low while underemployment is widespread
items.markingKey: Context (Around 80-90% of India's workforce is estimated to work in the informal economy.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: A student claims that unemployment only affects the people who lose their jobs. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: It also affects families, communities (crime, poorer health), firms (lower demand) and the government (lower tax revenue, higher spending).
items.markingKey: It also affects families, communities (crime, poorer health), firms (lower demand) and the government (lower tax revenue, higher spending). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: With the help of a labelled diagram, outline structural unemployment using a labour market diagram.
items.answer: In a declining industry, the demand for labour shifts left; with wage rigidity, the quantity of labour supplied exceeds demand; or a minimum wage set above equilibrium creates unemployment.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: In a declining industry, the demand for labour shifts left; with wage rigidity, the quantity of labour supplied exceeds demand; or a minimum wage set above equilibrium creates unemployment.
